source_text:
Ἡ τοῦ κυρίου παράδοσις ἣν μετὰ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς ἐνετείλατο προστάξας· Πορευθέντες μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου
πνεύματος. ∆ῆλον ὅτι τὴν ἐντολὴν ἐδεξάμεθα οὐ μόνον εἰς τὸ βαπτίζειν οὕτως, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς τὸ μαθητεύειν οὕτως, ὡς διὰ ταύτης τῆς ἐντολῆς καὶ τὴν Σαβελλίου νόσον ἀποκλεισθῆναι τῶν τριῶν ὑποστάσεων καθαρῶς ἡμῖν παραδοθεισῶν, καὶ τῶν Ἀνο μοίων καὶ τῶν Ἀρειανῶν καὶ τῶν Πνευματομάχων ἐμφραγῆναι τὰ στόματα τῶν μὲν προσώπων καὶ τῶν ὑποστάσεων τριῶν δηλου μένων, τῆς δὲ φύσεως καὶ τῆς θεότητος μιᾶς ὁμολογηθείσης. Ἀνάγκη τοίνυν οὕτως ἡμᾶς βαπτίζειν ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν, καὶ οὕτω πιστεύειν ὡς ἐβαπτίσθημεν, καὶ οὕτω δοξάζειν ὡς ἐπιστεύσαμεν. Πολλὰ γὰρ τῇ διανοίᾳ περισκοποῦντες καὶ πανταχοῦ στραφέντες τοῖς λογισμοῖς οὐδὲν ἐπινοῆσαι δυνάμεθα μεταξὺ τοῦ κτιστοῦ καὶ τῆς κτίσεως, ὥστε εἰ τῆς θεότητος τὸ πνεῦμα χωρίζομεν, ἀνάγκη μετὰ τῶν κτισμάτων αὐτὸ καταριθμεῖν. Εἰ δὲ κτίσμα τολμήσοιμεν εἰπεῖν, πῶς δυνατὸν ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι μιχθῆναι; Τὴν πολυθεΐαν οὕτως ὡς καὶ τὴν ἀθεΐαν κακίζομεν· καὶ οὔτε τρεῖς ἀρχὰς οὔτε τρεῖς θεοὺς οὔτε τρεῖς διαφόρους καταγγέλλομεν φύσεις, ἀλλὰ ἀρχὴν τῶν ὅλων τὸν πατέρα γινώσκοντες οὔτε τινὰ τῶν τριῶν ὑποστάσεων ἀθετοῦμεν καὶ τὸ σεμνὸν τῶν θείων γραφῶν καὶ τὰς ἐφ' ἕκαστον μαρτυρίας προσάγοντες.
thought_title: The Lord's command as the rule of baptism, faith, and doxology
orientation: Amphilochius is explaining that the Lord's baptismal command is the source of the faith, and he now quotes that command and draws out its anti-heretical force.
pass_a_gloss: The Lord's tradition, which after the resurrection from the dead he commanded to his holy disciples, having ordered: Going, make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. It is clear that we received the command not only to baptize thus, but also to make disciples thus, so that through this command both the disease of Sabellius was shut out, the three persons having been delivered to us clearly, and the mouths of the Anomoeans and of the Arians and of the opponents of the Spirit were stopped, the persons and the persons being three being made clear, and the nature and the Godhead being confessed as one. It is necessary therefore for us to baptize thus as we were taught, and to believe thus as we were baptized, and to glorify thus as we believed. For examining many things in the mind and having turned everywhere in our reasonings we are able to devise nothing between the creator and the creation, so that if we separate the Spirit from the Godhead, it is necessary to number him with the creatures. But if we should dare to say creature, how is it possible for him to be mixed in baptism? We denounce polytheism thus as also atheism; and we proclaim neither three first principles nor three gods nor three different natures, but knowing the Father as first principle of all things we neither reject any of the three persons and we bring forward the majesty of the divine scriptures and the testimonies for each one.

choices.why: Keeps the noun 'tradition' to match the source's emphasis on what was handed down, not merely a teaching.

choices.term: τῶν τριῶν ὑποστάσεων καθαρῶς ἡμῖν παραδοθεισῶν
choices.english: the three persons having been delivered to us clearly
choices.why: Uses the glossary rendering 'person' for hypostasis and keeps the passive participle's causal force.
rejected: the three hypostases having been handed down to us clearly

choices.term: τῆς δὲ φύσεως καὶ τῆς θεότητος μιᾶς ὁμολογηθείσης
choices.english: the nature and the Godhead being confessed as one
choices.why: Uses the glossary renderings 'nature' and 'Godhead' and preserves the singular feminine participle agreeing with both nouns.
rejected: the essence and divinity being confessed as one

choices.term: μεταξὺ τοῦ κτιστοῦ καὶ τῆς κτίσεως
choices.english: between the creator and the creation
choices.why: Uses the glossary renderings 'creator' and 'creation' and keeps the spatial metaphor of 'between'.
rejected: between the uncreated and the created order

choices.term: ἀνάγκη μετὰ τῶν κτισμάτων αὐτὸ καταριθμεῖν
choices.english: it is necessary to number him with the creatures
choices.why: Keeps the impersonal necessity construction and the verb 'number among' to show the consequence of separating the Spirit.
rejected: we must count him among the creatures

choices.why: Renders 'archai' as 'first principles' to distinguish from 'three gods' and 'three natures' in the same clause.

bible_refs.note: Πορευθέντες μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος

pass_b_english: The Lord's tradition is what he commanded his holy disciples after his resurrection from the dead, when he ordered them: "Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19). Clearly we received the command not only to baptize in this way, but also to make disciples in this way. Through this command the sickness of Sabellius is shut out, because the three persons have been delivered to us clearly, and the mouths of the Anomoeans, the Arians, and the opponents of the Spirit are stopped, because the persons and hypostases are shown to be three, while the nature and the Godhead are confessed as one. It is necessary, then, for us to baptize as we were taught, to believe as we were baptized, and to glorify as we believed. For however much we examine with our minds and turn our thoughts in every direction, we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation. So if we separate the Spirit from the Godhead, it is necessary to number him with the creatures. And if we dare to call him a creature, how can he be joined in baptism? We denounce polytheism just as we denounce atheism. We proclaim neither three first principles nor three gods nor three different natures, but we know the Father as the first principle of all things, we reject none of the three persons, and we bring forward the majesty of the divine Scriptures and the testimonies concerning each one.
notes: The source text has 'Ἀνο μοίων' split across a line break; it is the single word 'Ἀνομοίων' (Anomoeans).
The source text has 'δηλου μένων' split across a line break; it is the single word 'δηλουμένων' (being made clear).

last_rejected.quote: how can he be joined in baptism
last_rejected.source_quote: πῶς δυνατὸν ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι μιχθῆναι
last_rejected.why: μιχθῆναι means 'mixed' or 'mingled,' not 'joined'; baptism's coherence is lost.
last_rejected.fix: how can he be mixed in baptism
last_rejected.ruling: Greek μιχθῆναι = 'to be mixed'; 'joined' is a looser but acceptable rendering, not a major loss of meaning.

problems.quote: the persons and hypostases are shown to be three
problems.why: Intro says 'person' singular for each reality; text uses 'persons' plural for the three together. Reader may not connect these.
problems.fix: Clarify in intro that 'person' = each, 'persons' = all three.

problems.quote: the persons and hypostases are shown to be three
problems.why: No prior explanation that 'person' and 'hypostasis' are equivalent here; reader may think two different things.

problems.quote: For however much we examine with our minds and turn our thoughts in every direction, we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation.
problems.why: Sudden shift to first person plural without clear referent—synod? all Christians? rhetorical 'we'?
problems.fix: Clarify 'we' = the bishops of the synod.

problems.quote: We denounce polytheism just as we denounce atheism
problems.why: In context of defending Spirit's divinity, 'atheism' seems misplaced; likely means 'anarchy of belief' or denial of God's unity.
problems.fix: Check Greek; may mean 'we reject both division and denial of the Trinity'.

problems.quote: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit
problems.why: Cited as Matthew 28:19 but quotation includes 'Go and make disciples' which is v.19a, while 'baptizing' is v.19b; standard citation acceptable but wording blends elements.
problems.fix: Verify exact quotation matches preferred translation or note composite citation.

problems.why: Same group described differently; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Use one label, e.g., 'opponents of the Spirit,' in both places.

variants.text: those who, through blasphemy against the Spirit, incur the unforgivable sin

edits.old: the persons and hypostases are shown to be three
edits.new: the persons are shown to be three

edits.old: For however much we examine with our minds and turn our thoughts in every direction, we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation.
edits.new: For however much we bishops of the synod examine with our minds and turn our thoughts in every direction, we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation.

edits.old: We denounce polytheism just as we denounce atheism.
edits.new: We denounce polytheism just as we denounce atheism.

fixed: The English 'the persons and hypostases are shown to be three' is redundant because the source has 'τῶν προσώπων καὶ τῶν ὑποστάσεων τριῶν δηλουμένων' where both terms refer to the same three realities; the glossary already equates hypostasis with person, so 'persons' alone is sufficient.

The source 'Πολλὰ γὰρ τῇ διανοίᾳ περισκοποῦντες' has no explicit subject; the first-person plural is the author speaking for the synod, so clarifying 'we bishops of the synod' is a legitimate interpretive addition.
The source 'Τὴν πολυθεΐαν οὕτως ὡς καὶ τὴν ἀθεΐαν κακίζομεν' means 'We denounce polytheism just as we denounce atheism'; the English is accurate and needs no change.
The quotation is from Matthew 28:19 and the English accurately renders the Greek source; no change needed.
The English consistently uses 'opponents of the Spirit' for Πνευματομάχοι, matching the glossary; no change needed.

problems.quote: For however much we bishops of the synod examine with our minds and turn our thoughts in every direction, we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation.
problems.why: The shift to 'we bishops of the synod' is clear, but the rhetorical 'we' vs. earlier 'we' (synod) and 'I' (Amphilochius) could blur; actually acceptable.

problems.quote: we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation
problems.why: Should likely be 'we can conceive of nothing' or 'there is nothing'; 'devise' suggests invention rather than ontological possibility.
Cited correctly as baptismal formula; no mismatch.

problems.quote: the nature and the Godhead are confessed as one
problems.why: 'Godhead' and 'Trinity' alternate without signaling they refer to the same concept.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or clarify they are synonymous.

edits.old: we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation
edits.new: we can conceive of nothing between the creator and the creation

fixed: Speaker problem: no edit; the English 'we bishops of the synod' is acceptable and the source does not require a change.
Mistranslation: changed 'devise' to 'conceive of' to better reflect the ontological sense of ἐπινοῆσαι.
Wrong scripture: no edit; Matthew 28:19 is correctly cited.
Glossary: no edit; 'Godhead' is the required glossary term for θεότης and is used consistently here.
